Hi Alex -

Thanks for the clear questions - happy to confirm. I've summarized our standard hosted API behavior and the options available for AcmeHealth. I also attached the DPA and SOC2 for your legal team in the original thread.

Summary (Hosted API - default):
- Prompts & Outputs: By default we log request and response bodies (prompts and model outputs) for up to 30 days for debugging, abuse detection, and quality monitoring. After 30 days these request/response bodies are purged from Tier-1 logs.
- Metadata & Audit Logs: Non-content metadata (timestamps, request IDs, model, token counts, region, and anonymized usage metrics) are retained for 12 months for billing, analytics, and audit purposes. IP addresses are stored as truncated/anonymized values for up to 90 days.
- Use for Improvement: For customers on our hosted shared offering, prompts/outputs are not used to improve public models without an opt-in. We do use aggregated, anonymized usage statistics to monitor model health. Customers can opt out of any use for model improvement via the DPA.
- Searchability: Full request/response bodies are not exposed as a full-text searchable index in the product UI for customers beyond immediate debug/ops uses. Internal access is limited to engineers on a need-to-know basis and is audited.
- Data Residency: We run regionally segmented clusters (US, EU, APAC). Data stored for a customer is kept in the region(s) tied to the customer's account/tenant. For AcmeHealth we can scope your tenant to the US region (data stored in US-only data centers) or EU if you require EU residency.
- Encryption & Access: Data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated/Private offerings; hosted tenants use KMS keys managed by Redwood but with role-based access controls and regular key rotation.

Options for stricter controls (available under Dedicated or Private deployments):
- No-body-retention mode: In Dedicated and Private deployments we can enable a configuration where request/response bodies are not persisted to logs (ephemeral-only). This is the recommended path if you must guarantee no prompt/output retention.
- Contractual Controls: We can incorporate an explicit retention schedule, strict access controls, and audit rights into the DPA/Security Addendum.
- On-prem / VPC: If required, we support a Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) where all storage, logs, and keys remain under your control.

Practical next steps I suggest:
1) If you can confirm which residency you prefer (US), we will scope the tenant and note it in the DPA.
2) Sign the attached DPA to lock in opt-outs for model training and the retention guarantees.
3) If you want the no-body-retention configuration, we can schedule an engineering call to size Dedicated capacity or the Private deployment and produce a mutual action plan.

I'm happy to jump on a short call with your security team to walk through the technical controls. If helpful, you can also send a small set of representative prompts (redacted/anonymized) and we'll run them through the hosting flow and confirm what logs would contain.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
